scope_note: GitHub currently returns 25 PRs per page for pages 20-40. Pages 41-50 return no results because GitHub search pagination is limited to its first 1000 results.
counting_rule: Counts are conservative and include only independently resolved behavior, correctness, concurrency, safety, or compatibility problems. Pure refactors, formatting, test-only changes, and unresolved FIXME items are excluded.

problem_descriptions: get_cpuid_level() returned the TSC frequency denominator instead of the highest supported CPUID level.
get_clflush_size() returned the cache-line size without the required 8-byte scaling.
Signal-stack flags were handled without separating user-controlled flags from internally managed state.
Signal-stack settings were not preserved on the user stack and restored correctly by rt_sigreturn.
The handler_count-based active-stack tracking was incorrect when SS_AUTODISARM disabled the stack.
The CI workflow always forced release mode and KVM mode instead of honoring the requested debug configuration.
Receiving an empty UNIX SEQPACKET packet could trigger a kernel assertion failure.
pause_timeout() could miss a signal that arrived between signal setup and entering the wait.
Mountpoint state was cleared incorrectly when one dentry corresponded to multiple mounts.
Mount flags were not updated in all detach and mount-point replacement paths.
Shebang parsing rejected valid interpreter lines containing multiple arguments.
Whitespace after #! produced an incorrect empty interpreter argument.
MADV_NOHUGEPAGE caused a panic even though huge pages were unsupported.
capget did not implement the Linux behavior for an unsupported capability version with a null output address.
openat did not return ENOENT for an empty pathname.
ReadCString returned the wrong error when a string reached the user-space address limit without a NUL terminator.
Netlink attribute parsing stopped at an embedded NUL or required a NUL terminator when Linux permits the attribute to end at the reader boundary.
Netlink parsing errors could leave the reader at the wrong position or be swallowed instead of being reported.
Blocking FIFO open did not wait for both a reader and a writer.
FIFO read and write operations ignored the nonblocking flag.
FIFO status_flags were shared at the pipe level instead of being independent per file descriptor.
A typo in the mount-namespace changes caused CI failure.
switch_to_mnt_ns could reject a valid operation with EINVAL and did not combine mount-tree cloning with resolver update atomically.
Setting a non-mount namespace incorrectly reset the filesystem resolver.
A clone argument check was performed in the wrong place and could be skipped.
CloneArgs::check missed invalid flag combinations such as CLONE_SIGHAND without CLONE_VM.
clone3() did not validate the relationship and user-space range of stack and stack-size arguments.
find_reaper_process() could lose the ancestor during concurrent parent reaping instead of retrying.
The memory orderings for child-subreaper state were inconsistent with the required synchronization.
getrandom rejected or accepted flags incorrectly.
getrandom could perform an unbounded allocation based on user input.
getrandom did not permit short writes according to the expected interface behavior.
Run queues were accessed without IRQ-disabled locking, allowing a deadlock through the registered IRQ callback.
The init process was not woken after dead children were moved, leaving LTP wait/reap tests stuck.
procfs uid_map/gid_map output was formatted without the required field separation.
procfs meminfo computed MemFree from MemTotal - MemAvailable, producing nonsensical values.
MMIO allocation used an unnecessarily strict 4 GiB alignment and failed for valid low-memory layouts.
PIO allocation consumed the range during the existence check and then iterated an empty range, causing a later recycle assertion failure.
procfs used inconsistent process-table and cached-entry lock orders.
procfs acquired a mutex while holding the file-table spinlock, causing an atomic-mode violation.
procfs returned incorrect information after execve was performed by a non-main thread.
procfs returned incorrect information after the file table was unshared.
A task directory could remain visible after its thread exited.
MemfdFile lacked access-mode checks, which would become observable when reopening a memfd.
InodeHandle did not map O_PATH to the correct empty rights set.
sched_setattr incorrectly converted user-memory EFAULT into EINVAL.
sched_getattr performed an unbounded allocation from user-controlled size.
sched_getattr did not report the required size to userspace when returning E2BIG.
evdev lseek returned the wrong error code instead of ESPIPE.
evdev failed to update event counters when copying an event to userspace failed.
evdev skipped required validation when max_events was zero.
evdev's full-buffer handling could fail to enqueue SYN_DROPPED events.
evdev could deadlock when dropping the last EvdevFile reference while a lock was held.
evdev could enter atomic mode break by registering while the caller held the input-handler lock.
ext2 SuperBlock reconstruction dropped fields from RawSuperBlock and could corrupt metadata on write-back.
FsState was declared with values that did not support its Linux bit-flag semantics.
The recovery calculation for log_*_size was incorrect except for the accidental value 2.
The previous ktest fix used the wrong option and caused kernel tests not to run.
Merged Rust 2024 changes left code unformatted.
The Rust 2024 update left cargo doc/publish checks failing.
mmap flag combinations and error codes did not match the Linux contract.
MM syscalls inconsistently handled address/length alignment and integer-overflow validation.
msync and mprotect did not return ENOMEM when part of the requested range was unmapped.
madvise used an incorrect dummy implementation for MADV_DONTNEED.
madvise implemented MADV_FREE with incorrect semantics.
madvise used an incorrect dummy implementation for MADV_DONTFORK.
Corrupted ELF headers could trigger assertions instead of a normal load error.
Untrusted ELF memory and file ranges could overflow arithmetic.
ELF loading returned incorrect error codes for malformed input.
VM activation occurred too early, hiding interpreter/segment-load errors from userspace.
Using LOGGER in TDX release mode generated CMP instructions while accessing MMIO.
virtio PCI num_queues() generated CMP instructions while accessing MMIO.
The OSDK option was misspelled as --ktest, so kernel tests were not selected.
Non-OSDK crates were not checked in both cfg(test) and non-cfg(test) configurations, allowing warnings to escape validation.
Deleting sparse files could leave incorrect ext2 sparse-file state.
Reading a sparse block did not return zero directly.
Writing a sparse block did not dynamically allocate a disk block.
fallocate PunchHoleKeepSize did not preserve sparse-hole semantics.
lseek-based sparse block creation was unsupported.
ftruncate expansion did not create sparse blocks.
Inconsistent heap-lock/MM-lock ordering could deadlock while generating /proc/[pid]/maps.
Concurrent fork() and brk() could leave the child with an incorrect heap region.
Credential permission checks used effective-root status instead of CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID.
The implementation treated UID 0 as invalid even though it represents root.
setfsuid() and setfsgid() did not follow the required always-return-old-ID behavior.
setuid() and setgid() did not correctly report failure conditions.
